title: Collaborative AI Engineering: One Dev, Two Dozen Agents, Zero Alignment — Maggie Appleton, GitHub
talk_summary: Maggie Appleton argues that cheap agentic implementation has collapsed the planning/review window, pushing all alignment onto PRs where it performs badly, and that the real bottleneck is agreeing on what to build. She demos ACE, a prototype where each work session is a shared cloud micro-VM with a multiplayer chat, shared terminal/preview, and collaborative plan editing so humans and agents align before and during implementation.

takeaways.technique: Shared, human-editable plan artifact before implementation
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent writes a plan into a shared doc that teammates can co-edit (cursors, comments) and revise requirements in; only after agreement do they tell the agent 'do this' with that plan as context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can collaboratively edit it together. We can decide if we like this plan, if it's any good at all, if it achieves our intent

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent reads the whole human conversation in the session as prompt input, so discussion before 'at Ace, do it' becomes context; a dashboard summarizes teammates' recent work to reorient you.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The agent can also read our whole conversation. That is all input to the prompt.

takeaways.technique: One always-on cloud micro-VM per work session
takeaways.what_they_do: Each session is backed by a sandboxed cloud VM on its own git branch, so work is isolated, survives laptop close, and multiple people/agents share the same terminal and live preview.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each session is more than a chat channel though. It is also backed by a micro VM.

takeaways.technique: Session summary block for parallel work
takeaways.what_they_do: A summary panel in each session keeps you oriented on latest changes from you or others so you can switch between many parallel sessions without drowning in activity noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this keeps me up to date with the latest changes in this session... so that you don't get overwhelmed with the amount of noise

takeaways.technique: Align before implementation, not only at PR
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues review time for generated code has increased and PRs are a poor alignment surface, so move checkpoints earlier (plan review, shared context) rather than relying on the merge gate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we know the review time for generated code is actually increased... All those checkpoints now come after the implementation
